title: Homily II — Angels, healings and the washing of the body

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, col. 737 (PDF leaf 410)

source_text: Καὶ τί γίνεται; Στοιχείων, ὥς γέ μοι δοκεῖ, κίνησις καὶ ἀλλοίωσις, φωναί τε ψόφοι, καὶ πάταγοι, καὶ ἀγγέλων ὕμνοι ἐπάξιοι, προτρεχόντων, συμπροπεμπόντων, παρεπομένων· τῶν μὲν τῇ ἀμωμήτῳ καὶ παναγίᾳ ψυχῇ τὴν δορυφορίαν πληρούντων, καὶ πρὸς οὐρανὸν ἀνιούσῃ συνανιόντων, ἕως ὅτε τῷ θρόνῳ τῷ βασιλικῷ τὴν βασιλίδα παρέστησαν, τῶν δὲ, τὸ θεῖον καὶ ἱερὸν κυκλούντων σῶμα, καὶ ᾠδαῖς ἀγγελοπρεπέσιν ὑμνούντων τὴν Θεομήτορα. Τί δὲ οἱ παρεστῶτες τῷ παναγίῳ καὶ ἱερωτάτῳ σώματι; Φόβῳ τε καὶ πόθῳ, καὶ ἀγαλλιάσεως δάκρυσι τὸ θεῖον καὶ πανόλβιον περιστοιχίσαντες σκήνωμα, περιεπτύσσοντο, κατησπάζοντο ἅπαν μέλος, προσῆγον τῷ σώματι, ἐκ τῆς ἁφῆς ἁγιασμοῦ τε καὶ εὐλογίας πληρούμενοι. Τότε δὴ νόσοι μὲν ἐδραπέτευον, δαιμόνων στίφη ἐφυγαδεύοντο, πάντοθεν συνελαυνόμενα πρὸς μόνα τὰ καταχθόνια· ἀὴρ, αἰθήρ τε καὶ οὐρανὸς ἡγιάζοντο τῇ ἀναβάσει τοῦ πνεύματος, γῆ δὲ τῇ καταθέσει τοῦ σώματος. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἡ τοῦ ὕδατος φύσις τῆς εὐλογίας ἠμοίρησε· λούεται γὰρ ὕδατι καθαρῷ, οὐκ αὐτὴν καθαίροντι, ἁγνιζομένῳ δὲ μάλιστα. Ἐνταῦθα κωφοῖς μὲν ἡ ἀκοὴ ἀπηρτίζετο, χωλοῖς αἱ τῶν ποδῶν κατηρτίζοντο βάσεις, τυφλοῖς δὲ ἀνεκαινίζετο ἡ ὅρασις, ἁμαρτωλοῖς πίστει προσιοῦσι χειρόγραφα διεῤῥήγνυντο. Εἶτα τί; Σινδόσι καθαραῖς τὸ καθαρὸν ἐνειλίττεται σῶμα, καὶ κλίνῃ αὖθις ἡ βασιλὶς ἐπιτίθεται. Εἶτα λαμπάδες καὶ μύρα, ὕμνοι προπόμπιοι, ἀγγέλων μὲν ταῖς οἰκείαις γλώτταις μελῳδούντων ὕμνον τὸν αὐτοῖς προσφορώτατον, ἀποστόλων δὲ καὶ θεοφόρων Πατέρων ᾠδὰς ᾀδόντων θεοπρεπεῖς, καὶ κροτουμένας τῷ Πνεύματι.
pass_a_gloss: And what happens (γίνεται)? Of elements, as it seems to me at least, movement (κίνησις) and alteration, voices (φωναί) and noises (ψόφοι) and crashings (πάταγοι), and worthy (ἐπάξιοι) hymns (ὕμνοι) of angels (ἄγγελοι) running before, escorting, following; some fulfilling (πληρόω) the bodyguard for the unblemished and all-holy (παναγία) soul, and going up with [it] going up (ἄνειμι) to heaven (οὐρανός), until they presented the queen (βασιλίς) to the royal throne (θρόνος); others encircling (κυκλόω) the divine and sacred body, and hymning (ὑμνέω) the God-mother with angel-befitting odes (ᾠδαί). And what of those standing by the all-holy and most sacred body? With fear (φόβος) and longing (πόθος) and tears (δάκρυα) of exultation, having stood around the divine and all-blessed tabernacle (σκήνωμα), they embraced, they kissed every limb (μέλος), they brought [themselves/limbs] to (προσάγω) the body, being filled from the touch (ἁφή) with sanctification and blessing (εὐλογία). Then indeed diseases (νόσοι) ran away, throngs (στίφη) of demons were put to flight, being driven together from all sides to the subterranean [places] alone; air (ἀήρ), ether (αἰθήρ) and heaven were sanctified (ἁγιάζω) by the ascent of the spirit, and earth by the deposition of the body. But not even the nature (φύσις) of water was without share (ἀμοιρέω) of the blessing; for she is washed (λούω) with pure (καθαρός) water, not cleansing (καθαίρω) her, but rather being purified (ἁγνίζω). There for the deaf (κωφοί) hearing (ἀκοή) was completed (ἀπαρτίζω), for the lame (χωλοί) the steps (βάσεις) of the feet were set right, for the blind (τυφλοί) sight (ὅρασις) was renewed, for sinners approaching (πρόσειμι) in faith (πίστις) handwritten bonds were torn apart. Then what? In pure linen cloths (σινδόνες) the pure body is wrapped, and on a couch/bier (κλίνη) again the queen is placed. Then torches (λαμπάδες) and ointments (μύρα), escorting hymns, angels in their own tongues (γλῶτται) singing (μελῳδέω) the hymn most suited to them, apostles and God-bearing (θεοφόροι) fathers (Πατέρες) singing (ᾄδω) God-befitting odes, struck/sounded (κροτέω) by the Spirit (Πνεῦμα).
pass_b_english: And what happens? A stirring and changing of the elements, as it seems to me at least; voices and sounds and crashes, and fitting hymns of angels, as they run ahead, escort her and follow after. Some formed a guard of honour for the blameless and all-holy soul and went up with it as it went up to heaven, until they presented the Queen at the royal throne; others encircled the divine and sacred body and hymned the Mother of God in songs fit for angels.

And what of those who stood beside the all-holy and most sacred body? With fear and longing and tears of joy they ranged themselves around that divine and all-blessed tabernacle; they embraced it, they kissed every limb, they pressed close to the body, and from its touch they were filled with holiness and blessing. Then diseases fled away, and swarms of demons were put to flight, driven together from every side into the regions under the earth, and there alone. Air, ether and heaven were sanctified by the ascent of her spirit, and earth by the laying down of her body. Nor did the nature of water go without a share in the blessing, for she is washed in pure water, which does not cleanse her but is rather itself made pure. Here hearing was restored to the deaf, the lame were made firm on their feet, sight was renewed for the blind, and for sinners who drew near in faith the records of their debts were torn up (Colossians 2:14).

What then? The pure body is wrapped in pure linen cloths, and the Queen is laid once more upon a bier. Then come torches and perfumes and hymns of escort: the angels singing in their own tongues the hymn most fitting for them, and the apostles and God-bearing fathers singing songs worthy of God, struck up by the Spirit.

choices.note: χειρόγραφα (handwritten bonds of debt) echoes Colossians 2:14 (the χειρόγραφον against us, blotted out), so it is cited; plural rendered "the records of their debts".
The list of deaf, lame and blind healed is general miracle language (compare Matthew 11:5;
Isaiah 35:5-6) and is not quoted; left uncited.
"Pure body wrapped in pure linen" may recall Joseph's wrapping of Christ's body in clean linen (Matthew 27:59); possible parallel, left uncited.
προσῆγον τῷ σώματι has no object in the Greek; rendered "they pressed close to the body".
The PG Latin takes ἅπαν μέλος with it ("applying every limb [of their own] to the body"); the Greek word order allows "they kissed every limb" as rendered.
σκήνωμα rendered "tabernacle" for the body throughout Homily II.
τὴν δορυφορίαν πληρούντων ("fulfilling the bodyguard") rendered "formed a guard of honour".
κροτουμένας τῷ Πνεύματι ("struck" or "sounded", as an instrument is played) rendered "struck up by the Spirit"; the PG Latin has "a Spiritu sancto inspiratas".
ἁγιαζομένῳ ("being sanctified"; little change in sense).
